per_query.question: What is the mode of action and IRAC resistance group of abamectin?
per_query.answer:
The mode of action of abamectin is a glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluCl) allozyme modulator that affects insect nerve and muscle action. Activation of glutamate-gated chloride channels after aliasing causes paralysis. [D1]

The IRAC resistance group of abamectin is IRAC Group 6; Avermectins. [D1]

per_query.question: What is the active substance of Sparta, and what is its mode of action?
per_query.answer:
The active substance of Sparta is spinetoram. The mode of action of spinetoram involves acting as a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) allosteric modulator-binding site I, affecting insect neural action. Allelic activation of its receptor (different from binding site-II of group 32) causes hyperexcitability of the insect nervous system. Acetylcholine is the main excitatory neurotransmitter in the insect central nervous system. [D1]

[D1]: New Zealand pesticide dataset

per_query.question: Sparta contains which active substance, and what introduction does the corpus give for that substance?
per_query.answer: Sparta contains the active substance spinetoram. The introduction given in the corpus for spinetoram is as follows: Spinetoram is an active substance produced by fermentation of secondary metabolites of the actinomycete Saccharopolyspora spinosa and chemically modified. It is an alternative product to polymyxin. In the rhamnose 3-position in the chemical structure of polymyxin, the insecticidal activity is increased by 10 times after the natural methyl ether is changed to ethyl ether, and the active ingredient in the original drug is a mixture of ethyl polymyxin-J and ethyl polymyxin-L (the ratio is about 70~90:30~10). This modification mainly results in the control of Lepidoptera and Tassel-winged insect pests. [D1]
